Class OffscreenAPI

java.lang.Object
com.sbancuz.offscreen.api.OffscreenAPI
public final class OffscreenAPI extends Object
The entry point for opening and controlling independent desktop GUI windows.

Think of a window as a small extra screen next to Minecraft. A HostUI teaches that window how to draw a particular GUI and deliver input to it. UIRegistry chooses that adapter when you supply a screen object.

Call this API on Minecraft's main client thread. These methods do not queue work from background threads, and creating a window needs an initialized SDL video backend and Minecraft OpenGL context. A concurrent registry does not make native window operations safe on arbitrary threads.

Use open(Supplier) for local screens. A GUI whose buttons or slots communicate with the server must use its synchronized factory, such as OffscreenSimpleFactory. Creating another visual window does not create another server container.

Here, MyClientScreen stands for a screen class supplied by your addon. The first-window walkthrough includes a complete GuiScreen example and its imports. 

Window window = OffscreenAPI.open(() -> new MyClientScreen());
if (OffscreenAPI.isOpen(window)) {
    OffscreenAPI.setTitle(window, "My addon");
    OffscreenAPI.resize(window, 960, 640);
}

Keep the window reference in your client code. In a later client action, close it when it is no longer needed: 

OffscreenAPI.close(window);

  • Method Details

    • open

      @Nullable public static Window open(Supplier<?> screenFactory)
      Creates a screen and opens it through the nearest registered adapter.

      The supplier runs immediately and exactly once. An unsupported or absent screen returns before allocating a native window. The initial title is the screen's toString(); use setTitle(Window, String) to replace it. Directly hosting GuiInventory is rejected by the window, so check isOpen(Window) before treating the returned object as usable. Supplier and adapter-factory exceptions propagate to the caller; they are not converted to null results.

      Parameters:
      screenFactory - non-null supplier of a fresh client-only screen
      Returns:
      the created window, or null if the supplier or adapter returned null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if screenFactory is null
      IllegalStateException - if native window/context creation fails

    • open

      @Nullable public static <H extends HostUI> Window open(Supplier<?> screenFactory, HostUIFactory<H> factory)
      Opens a local screen using an explicitly supplied adapter factory.

      This bypasses registry lookup, which is useful for one special screen. Supplier/factory exceptions propagate to the caller. The same client-thread, native-context and inventory restrictions as open(Supplier) apply.

      Type Parameters:
      H - adapter type produced by the factory
      Parameters:
      screenFactory - non-null screen supplier, invoked immediately once
      factory - adapter factory, required when the supplier returns a screen
      Returns:
      the window, or null if either creation step returns null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if a required supplier or factory is null
      IllegalStateException - if native window/context creation fails

    • close

      public static void close(@Nullable Window window)
      Releases a window and, if present, its server-bound session.

      The session gets the first chance to release its framework/network binding. It untracks itself before closing the native window, preventing recursive disposal. Calling this again after closure is harmless.

      Parameters:
      window - window to close; null does nothing

    • closeImmediately

      public static void closeImmediately(@Nullable Window window)
      Releases a session and its native window without running a visual exit. Use on the client thread for reload, world teardown or failed initialization. Closure requested inside a borrowed render callback completes when that callback returns; its resources remain valid until then.
      Parameters:
      window - exact owner, or null

    • closeAll

      public static void closeAll()
      Destroys every window currently tracked by the client driver. Registered sessions observe their closed windows during maintenance. Use close(Window) when a specific session should be released immediately.

    • closeAll

      public static void closeAll(@Nullable Predicate<Window> predicate)
      Destroys tracked windows accepted by a filter, leaving other windows alone. The filter executes on the caller's thread; its exceptions propagate.

      Like closeAll(), this destroys windows directly. Use close(Window) to release a window's registered session before starting window cleanup.

      Parameters:
      predicate - selection rule; null closes nothing

    • setIcon

      public static boolean setIcon(@Nullable Window window, net.minecraft.util.ResourceLocation resource) throws IOException
      Sets a per-window desktop icon from the current client resource packs. Example: new ResourceLocation("my_addon", "textures/gui/window_icon.png"). The PNG lives at assets/my_addon/textures/gui/window_icon.png; use a square image such as 32 or 64 pixels with transparency. Navigation and synchronized retries keep the icon because they reuse the same native window. Native title-bar/taskbar presentation and application grouping remain controlled by the operating system.
      Parameters:
      window - native owner; null or closed returns false without reading the resource
      resource - client resource location, never a filesystem path
      Returns:
      true if SDL accepted the image, false if unavailable or unsupported
      Throws:
      IOException - if the resource is absent or is not a readable image
      IllegalArgumentException - for an image larger than 1024 pixels on either axis

    • isOpen

      public static boolean isOpen(@Nullable Window window)
      Checks whether a window still has a native handle and is not being destroyed. An OS close request can remain pending until the next update/render pass. For a synchronized window, this can return true before its server-provided panel arrives.
      Parameters:
      window - candidate window; null is treated as closed
      Returns:
      true while the native window is open

    • push

      public static void push(@Nullable Window window, @Nullable HostUI ui)
      Places an adapted child screen above the current screen in a window. The parent remains underneath and is shown again when the child is popped.

      Use a fresh adapter and backing screen for each stack entry. Popping an entry disposes its adapter, so sharing that adapter with another entry or window would leave the other owner using a disposed object. Once pushed, let the window dispose it. If window is null, nothing is pushed and ownership stays with the caller.

      Parameters:
      window - open destination window; null does nothing
      ui - child adapter whose disposal is now owned by the window; null does nothing

    • push

      public static void push(@Nullable Window window, @Nullable Supplier<?> screenFactory)
      Creates and adapts a child screen before placing it on the window's stack. Missing screens or adapters leave the existing stack unchanged. Supplier and adapter-factory exceptions propagate to the caller.
      Parameters:
      window - open destination window; null skips supplier execution
      screenFactory - immediate supplier of a fresh child screen; null does nothing

    • pop

      public static boolean pop(@Nullable Window window)

    • getCurrentUI

      @Nullable public static HostUI getCurrentUI(@Nullable Window window)
      Reads the adapter at the top of a window's navigation stack. This borrows the adapter; callers must not independently dispose it or push it into another stack entry. Navigation can dispose the adapter while a caller still holds this reference.
      Parameters:
      window - window to inspect, possibly null
      Returns:
      current adapter, or null for no window or an empty stack

    • setClearColor

      public static void setClearColor(@Nullable Window window, float r, float g, float b, float a)
      Sets the color used to clear the rendering surface before drawing the GUI. This is not a promise of operating-system window transparency.

      The hosted screen draws over this color. A screen that paints an opaque background can cover it completely.

      Parameters:
      window - destination window; null does nothing
      r - red component, normally 0 to 1
      g - green component, normally 0 to 1
      b - blue component, normally 0 to 1
      a - alpha component, normally 0 to 1

    • setClearColor

      public static void setClearColor(@Nullable Window window, int argb)
      Sets the clear color using four packed bytes in 0xAARRGGBB order. For example, 0xFFFF0000 is red with full alpha: FF alpha, FF red, 00 green, and 00 blue.
      Parameters:
      window - destination window; null does nothing
      argb - alpha, red, green, and blue, each occupying eight bits
      See Also:
      • setClearColor(Window, float, float, float, float)

    • setBackground

      public static void setBackground(@Nullable Window window, @Nullable Runnable background)
      Installs a drawing callback behind the hosted GUI. The callback runs during window rendering on the client thread; keep it short and do not move its OpenGL work to a background thread.

      It runs after the surface is cleared and before the normal GUI projection is installed. Set up the projection and drawing state the callback needs. The hosted screen draws afterward and can cover the result with its own opaque background.

      Parameters:
      window - destination window; null does nothing
      background - drawing callback, or null to remove the custom background
